---
title: Keep a copy in sync with the event stream
sidebar_label: Keep a copy in sync
description: Follow an instance's event stream from a cursor, so a copy of your data stays current and picks up where it stopped after a break.
job: A builder follows the event stream from a cursor so their copy stays current and resumes after a break.
---

A search index, a cache or a report keeps its own copy of an instance's data. Read it once, then apply each change from the [event stream](/build/events) and save a cursor, so after a break you receive everything you missed and nothing twice. A [working copy](/build/working-copies) does this for the Swift SDK.

You need a key that reads `core.file` and its subtypes ([Manage keys](/use/manage-keys)) in `MARFA_API_KEY`, and your instance's address in `MARFA_API_URL`.

## What the stream sends

From cursor `21`, narrowed to files, `marfa events` prints one frame a line:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa events --type core.file --edges none --cursor 21
```

```text
-  stream_cursor  25
22  item.created  01a1f126-5ad1-7029-8f69-a66a15ee406d
23  item.trashed  01a1f124-12c1-7762-af28-52450dd463af
25  item.purged  01a1f124-12c1-7762-af28-52450dd463af
-  stream_live  25
```

</Terminal>

Over HTTP, [the stream](/reference/api/event-stream/streamEvents) takes your cursor in `Last-Event-ID` and answers server-sent events. It opens with `stream_cursor`, the **head of the log**, replays every event after your cursor, sends `stream_live` once caught up, then sends each new event. Only events carry an `id:` line, so **the last `id:` you received is always a cursor you can resume from**.

## Build the sync

A browser `EventSource` can't send an `Authorization` header and the [TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk) doesn't read streams, so read it with `fetch`, and take each frame as it arrives: Marfa closes a reader that takes nothing for 30 seconds.

```ts title="sync.ts"
const baseUrl = process.env.MARFA_API_URL!;
const credential = process.env.MARFA_API_KEY!;

async function* frames(cursor?: string) {
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/events?type=core.file&edges=none`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${credential}`, ...(cursor && { "Last-Event-ID": cursor }) },
  });
  if (!response.ok || !response.body) throw new Error(`The stream answered ${response.status}`);
  let buffer = "";
  for await (const text of response.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream())) {
    const blocks = (buffer + text).split("\n\n");
    buffer = blocks.pop() ?? "";
    for (const block of blocks) {
      const frame = { id: "", event: "message", data: "" };
      for (const line of block.split("\n")) {
        const [, field, value] = /^([^:]+):\s?(.*)$/.exec(line) ?? [];
        if (field === "id" || field === "event" || field === "data") frame[field] = value;
      }
      if (frame.data) yield frame;
    }
  }
}
```

**Save the cursor in the same place as the copy, in step with what you apply.** An item event carries the item as it stands after the change, so `apply` replaces what the copy holds, or removes it for `item.purged`. `item.trashed` keeps it, in the bin.

```ts title="sync.ts"
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createClient, pages, type components } from "@withmarfa/client";

const marfa = createClient({ baseUrl, credential });
type Item = components["schemas"]["Item"];
let copy: { cursor?: string; files: Record<string, Item> } =
  await readFile("files-copy.json", "utf8").then(JSON.parse, () => ({ files: {} }));

function apply(event: { event_type: string; item: Item }) {
  if (event.event_type === "item.purged") delete copy.files[event.item.id];
  else if (event.event_type.startsWith("item.") || event.event_type === "metadata.changed") {
    copy.files[event.item.id] = event.item;
  }
}

async function saveCursor(cursor: string) {
  copy.cursor = cursor;
  await writeFile("files-copy.json", JSON.stringify(copy));
}
```

`follow` applies each event, saves its ID, and returns the frame that ended the stream. It saves the `cursor` of `stream_live` too, because on a narrow stream the last event can be far behind the head.

```ts title="sync.ts"
async function follow(cursor: string): Promise<string> {
  for await (const frame of frames(cursor)) {
    const data = JSON.parse(frame.data);
    if (frame.event === "stream_cursor") continue;
    if (frame.event === "stream_live") await saveCursor(data.cursor);
    else if (["stream_incomplete", "catchup_too_old", "cursor_ahead"].includes(frame.event)) return frame.event;
    else {
      apply(data);
      await saveCursor(frame.id);
    }
  }
  return "closed";
}
```

`rebuild` takes the head of the log from the first frame, lists every file in every state, then saves the head as the cursor, so each change made while it lists waits in the log. The loop resumes from the saved cursor after a break, and rebuilds when the cursor can't be used:

```ts title="sync.ts"
async function rebuild(): Promise<string> {
  let head = "";
  for await (const frame of frames()) {
    if (frame.event !== "stream_cursor") throw new Error("The stream didn't name the head of the log");
    head = JSON.parse(frame.data).cursor;
    break; // the first frame names the head, and breaking closes the stream
  }
  copy = { files: {} };
  const files = pages(async (cursor) => {
    const { data, error } = await marfa.GET("/items", { params: { query: { type: "core.file", state: "any", cursor } } });
    if (error) throw new Error(error.error.message);
    return data;
  });
  for await (const item of files) apply({ event_type: "item.created", item: item as Item });
  await saveCursor(head);
  return head;
}

let cursor = copy.cursor;
for (;;) {
  cursor ??= await rebuild();
  const ended = await follow(cursor);
  cursor = ended === "catchup_too_old" || ended === "cursor_ahead" ? undefined : copy.cursor;
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
}
```

Run it as an ES module and add a file with `marfa items add`: the copy follows.

## When the stream ends

| You see | It means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The connection closes with no frame | A network fault, or your reader took nothing for 30 seconds. | Resume from your saved cursor. |
| `stream_incomplete` | The stream couldn't go on, for its `reason`. | Resume from your saved cursor; for `credential_ended`, with a valid key. |
| `catchup_too_old` | The log no longer holds the events after your cursor. It keeps them 30 days by default. | Rebuild from the head of the log. |
| `cursor_ahead` | Your cursor is past the head, as after a restore from a backup. | Discard the cursor and rebuild. |

A refusal before the stream opens is a fault in the key or request, except `429 rate_limited`, which asks you to wait the seconds `Retry-After` names, and `503 stream_capacity_exhausted`, which asks you to try later. `marfa events` exits `1` for `cursor_ahead` and `catchup_too_old`, `3` for a `stream_incomplete` a new stream can mend, and `5` for `credential_ended` ([Exit codes](/reference/cli#exit-codes)).

## Narrow the stream, or catch up by listing

`type` takes up to ten types or patterns, such as `app.*`, each with its subtypes, and a cursor works under any filter. Edge events come whatever `type` says, so `sync.ts` sends `edges=none`.

To catch up without the stream, list with `updated_after` set to the latest `updated_at` you hold. The bound includes items changed at that instant, so **skip the ones you already hold by `id`**. This listing is always oldest change first, and it can't report a purged item; the stream can.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items list --updated-after 2026-11-19T00:11:32.554Z
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /items?updated_after=2026-11-19T00:11:32.554Z
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

The rules are in the [events](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/events.md) chapter of the contract.
